title: Ada bar bar Chana
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:3: Ada bar bar Chana, Geniva, in the name of Rav. In Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 16:6, Ada bar bar Chana brought a divorce document and lost it. Hyman suggests that both passages should read Abba, whom he identifies with Rabbah bar bar Chana. He refers to Bava Metzia 19a, where a divorce document was lost.

notes.text: The first reporting chain is compressed and does not expressly state every link between Ada and Geniva. The supplied אירכם is read with Bava Metzia19a אירכס, “was lost”; the preceding page names Rabbah bar bar Chana. Hyman proposes Abba rather than Ada.

The saved whole Venice Berakhot5:3 scalar has Ada bar bar Chana, Geniva, in Rav’s name without an explicit intermediate connector. Whole Venice Yevamot16:6 has Ada bringing and losing the divorce document. These attest Hyman’s Ada forms, not his proposal that both should read Abba or identify with Rabbah bar bar Chana. The earlier BavaMetzia19a lost-document consultation is inherited, not newly read; supplied אירכם versus named אירכס is not newly proved glyph history. Leading ב is contextual in, not a count of two instances.

The printed Hyman page has שאירכס, “was lost,” where the supplied transcription reads שאירכם. The consulted Bava Metzia passage names Rabbah bar bar Chana at the end of 18b and continues on 19a with the loss and recovery of his divorce document. The two Venetian Jerusalem Talmud passages have Ada. The Berakhot chain leaves the link between Ada and Geniva unstated. The Bava Metzia parallel is the one Hyman adduces for his proposed correction and identification.
